Faithful scoped actual-phase integration restatement:
E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. V:E→R is C2; kappa>=1 and kappa^-1||v||²<=D²V(x)[v,v]<=||v||² for every x,v (normalized beta=1).
J>=2; h>0; actual t_i=h/2(1-cos(i*pi/(J-1))), i=0,...,J-1; ell_j=Lagrange.basis(univ,t,j); Lambda=sup_{s∈[0,h]}sum_j|ell_j(s)|; omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i}(t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds; pw is the final omega row and b_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds. Assume only h²Lambda<=1; h<=1 is derived.
0<eta<=c<1 and eps>0. c is a contraction upper-bound parameter in the cost certificate, not an algorithm parameter or additional gradient query.
nu is the actual incoming phase-state probability measure. xstar∈E satisfies gradient V(xstar)=0; M>=0. The real function ||X-xstar||²+||P||² is nu-integrable and its nu-expectation is <=M. These actual-state moment hypotheses are explicit; no TV approximation or independently sampled proxy law is substituted.
gamma=((stdGaussian(E) prod stdGaussian(E)) prod (gi prod gi)), where gi=Measure.pi_{Fin J}(stdGaussian(E)); all four factors and each array coordinate are independent. mu=nu prod gamma. Write w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)) and P0=aP+sigma*zeta0.
For any f:E→E define Y0_i=X+t_iP0, Z0_f,j=gradient V(f(Y0_j)+sqrt(eta)G0_j), Y1_f,i=Y0_i-sum_j omega_ij Z0_f,j, Z1_f,j=gradient V(f(Y1_f,j)+sqrt(eta)G1_j) and Phi_f(w)=(X+hP0-sum_j pw_j Z1_f,j, a(P0-sum_j b_j Z1_f,j)+sigma*zeta1). The exact and approximate branches have their own Y1_f. For the constructed q,N set T(w)=2J+sum_i[(N(Y0_i(w))+1)+(N(Y1_q,i(w))+1)].
Set d=finrank_R E, S=h²Lambda/2, MR=M+(1-exp(-h))*d, B=6MR+3eps²+3eta*d, C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c), L0=C*(1+log(1+sqrt(2MR)/eps)) and L1=C*(1+log(1+sqrt(4MR+2S²B)/eps)). W_rho(mu1,mu2) is [inf_{pi coupling(mu1,mu2)} integral (sqrt(||DX||²+||DP||²))^rho dpi]^(1/rho), expressed in extended nonnegative reals, for every finite real rho>=1.
There exist one measurable exact optimality map p, one measurable stopped output map q and one measurable N:E→Nat such that p(y)+eta*gradient V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps, p is nonexpansive and the actual residual-stopped interpreter from y returns some(q(y),N(y)+1) with sufficient fuel N(y)+1. The identical p,q,N define actual full-phase Markov Kp,Kq, the actual output Phi_q and the actual total returned gradient count T. For every state s and finite real rho>=1, true Euclidean W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s))<=3hLambda eps. Under the same actual driving law mu=nu prod gamma, T is measurable, real-integrable and E_mu[T]<=J(2+L0+L1). For every driving input w the counted phase interpreter with fuel(y)=N(y)+1 returns exactly some(Phi_q(w),T(w)). All output/count/kernel/cost conjuncts share these witnesses.
One successful exact-real source two-layer phase with actual integral coefficients and all four Gaussian factors, joining real accuracy and expected returned query cost. The exact comparison phase uses exact proximal stochastic gradients, not deterministic gradient V_eta. N(y)+1 is a sufficient execution certificate, not a free runtime computation of N. Counts include terminal residual tests and 2J shifted noisy-gradient calls; arithmetic, random draws and failed-run cost are separate. No TV-to-unbounded-cost transfer. Run-wideD3 contraction/history/D7/D8, B2/depth-K/logarithmic Lambda/weight positivity/source parameter choices/smoothing/Wp/proxy-warmness/initialization/PBPS/main results and actual-input composition remain open.

blind_reconstruction.text:
Let E be any complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Let J be a natural number with J>=2. Let V:E->R be genuinely twice continuously Frechet differentiable, and let kappa be a nonnegative real with kappa>=1. Assume, for all x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Fix real eta,c,epsilon with 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Let nu be a probability measure on E x E and fix xstar in E with grad V(xstar)=0. Fix h,M in R with h>0 and M>=0. Assume that s=(X,P) -> ||X-xstar||^2+||P||^2 is Bochner integrable with respect to nu, with its integral <=M.
For the J actual indices i,j in Fin(J)={0,...,J-1}, define precisely
  t_i=(h/2)(1-cos((i/(J-1))pi)),
  ell_j(X)=product_{k in Fin(J),k!=j} (t_j-t_k)^(-1)(X-t_k),
  Lambda=sup{sum_j |ell_j(s)| : s in [0,h]},
  omega_ij=integral_0^{t_i} (t_i-s)ell_j(s) ds,
  pw_j=omega_{J-1,j},
  bw_j=integral_0^h ell_j(s) ds,
  S=(h^2/2)Lambda.
Here the quotient in the node formula is real; the ell_j are real Lagrange polynomials evaluated at real s; Lambda is the real supremum of the displayed interval image; all interval integrals use real Lebesgue measure with orientation. pw,bw denote positionWeight,momentumWeight.
Write D=dim_R E, a=exp(-h/2), sigma=sqrt(1-exp(-h)). Let G be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on E. Set gi=product_{Fin(J)} G, gamma=(G x G) x (gi x gi), and mu=nu x gamma. All noise factors are independent: two E-valued Gaussian vectors and two independent J-coordinate Gaussian arrays whose own coordinates are independent. Under mu the incoming state of law nu is independent of this noise. Define exactly
  MR=M+(1-exp(-h))D,
  B=6 MR+3 epsilon^2+3 eta D,
  C=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c),
  L0=C[1+log(1+sqrt(2 MR)/epsilon)],
  L1=C[1+log(1+sqrt(4 MR+2 S^2 B)/epsilon)].
If h^2 Lambda<=1, there exist single global measurable maps p,q:E->E and N:E->N such that, for every y in E,
  p(y)+eta grad V(p(y))=y,
  ||q(y)-p(y)||<=epsilon,
  proximalQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1),
and p is nonexpansive: ||p(u)-p(v)||<=||u-v|| for all u,v in E.
The interpreter proximalQuery(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) returns none at zero fuel. With fuel n+1 it evaluates g(x), sets z=y-eta g(x), and tests ||z-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon. On success it returns some(x,1); otherwise it recurses at z with fuel n, propagates failure and increments a successful count by one. The equivalent residual threshold is ||x+eta g(x)-y||<=(1-eta)epsilon. The terminal successful gradient/residual test is counted. N(y)+1 is a finite successful execution certificate with no claim of free precomputation of the fuel/count.
For those same p,q,N and full input w=((X,P),((zeta0,zeta1),(G0,G1))), define the approximate phase by
  P0(w)=a P+sigma zeta0,
  Y0_i(w)=X+t_i P0(w),
  Z0_j(w)=grad V(q(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0_j(w),
  Z1_j(w)=grad V(q(Y1_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phi(w)=(X+h P0(w)-sum_j pw_j Z1_j(w),
          a(P0(w)-sum_j bw_j Z1_j(w))+sigma zeta1),
  T(w)=2J+sum_i[(N(Y0_i(w))+1)+(N(Y1_i(w))+1)] in N.
Define the exact implicit-map phase, using the same P0,Y0 and supplied noise coordinates, by
  Z0p_j(w)=grad V(p(Y0_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G0_j),
  Y1p_i(w)=Y0_i(w)-sum_j omega_ij Z0p_j(w),
  Z1p_j(w)=grad V(p(Y1p_j(w))+sqrt(eta)G1_j),
  Phip(w)=(X+h P0(w)-sum_j pw_j Z1p_j(w),
           a(P0(w)-sum_j bw_j Z1p_j(w))+sigma zeta1).
In particular the exact second stage uses Y1p, not the approximate Y1.
On the state space Q=E x E use the explicit distance
  d2((X,P),(Xprime,Pprime))=sqrt(||X-Xprime||^2+||P-Pprime||^2).
For real rho and measures alpha,beta on Q define the extended-nonnegative quantity
  W_rho(alpha,beta)=[inf_{tau measure on Q x Q: tau.fst=alpha,tau.snd=beta}
                       integral^- (ENNReal.ofReal(d2(s,sprime)))^rho dtau(s,sprime)]^(rho^(-1)).
This is the infimum over all coupling measures with the two specified marginals of the lower integral of the powered cost, followed by the inverse-rho real power. ENNReal.ofReal embeds max(real value,0); powers are real powers in extended nonnegative reals. The metric is the displayed square-root sum of squared position and momentum norms, not an unspecified default product norm.
Then Phi and T are measurable, and there exist Markov kernels Kp,Kq:Q->Q with probability outputs satisfying, simultaneously,
  Kp(s)=(z -> Phip(s,z))_* gamma for every incoming s,
  Kq(s)=(z -> Phi(s,z))_* gamma for every incoming s,
  phaseQuery(grad V,eta,epsilon,h,t,omega,pw,bw,(y -> N(y)+1),w)
    =some(Phi(w),T(w)) for every full input w,
  w -> (T(w):R) is Bochner integrable under mu,
  integral (T(w):R) dmu(w) <= (J:R)(2+L0+L1),
  W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s)) <= ENNReal.ofReal(3 h Lambda epsilon)
    for every incoming state s and every real rho>=1.
phaseQuery is the supplied Option-valued finite program. In increasing Fin(J) order it executes the same proximalQuery at each first-stage Y0_i with fuel(Y0_i), anchor and initial iterate Y0_i. It maps a successful point/count (x,n) to (grad V(x+sqrt(eta)G0_i),n+1), collecting these actual gradient values and adding counts. Any failure returns none. It constructs second-stage inputs using the actually returned first gradients, then repeats the corresponding second array with G1, charging one shifted-gradient evaluation in addition to each actual proximal count. It returns the resulting full position/momentum state and the sum of both array counts. Thus T counts every actual interpreter evaluation, including each terminal successful test, plus one additional shifted-gradient query per node per stage, totaling an overhead of exactly 2J. No desired output or count is given as input to phaseQuery.
All sums range over the J actual nodes. The integral count bound uses precisely mu=nu x gamma, whereas the transport bound compares both one-step output laws at the same arbitrary incoming state and holds for every real rho>=1, including noninteger exponents with no upper restriction. These conclusions share the same witnesses p,q,N and kernels Kp,Kq. No assertion is made about an optimal coupling being attained, a free fuel-selection algorithm, elapsed time, sampler invariance or long-run convergence, comparison with a continuous-time dynamics, or the growth of Lambda.

import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.SourceQuadratureWork
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalPhaseStability
import AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.ProximalExecutionIdentity

/-! Same stopped interpreter and actual source phase: precision and expected
query work are proved for identical witnesses under the genuine driving law.
One phase only; neither main theorem nor TV-based unbounded cost transfer. -/
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped NNReal BigOperators
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PhaseAccuracyWork
variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- The actual source-coefficient stopped phase has both Euclidean all-rho
precision and integrable expected returned gradient counts for the same p,q,N. -/
theorem source_phase_accuracy_and_work {J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) {V : E → ℝ} {κ : ℝ≥0}
    (hκ : 1 ≤ κ) (hV : ContDiff ℝ 2 V)
    (hH : ∀ x v : E, (κ : ℝ)⁻¹ * ‖v‖^2 ≤ (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ ‖v‖^2)
    {eta c eps : ℝ} (heta : 0 < eta) (hec : eta ≤ c) (hc : c < 1) (heps : 0 < eps)
    (ν : Measure (E × E)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (xstar : E) (hstar : gradient V xstar = 0)
    {h M : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) (hM : 0 ≤ M)
    (hstateI : Integrable (fun s : E × E => ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2) ν)
    (hstate : (∫ s : E × E, ‖s.1-xstar‖^2 + ‖s.2‖^2 ∂ν) ≤ M)
:
    let t := fun i : Fin J => h/2*(1-Real.cos ((i : ℝ)/(J-1 : ℝ)*Real.pi))
    let ell := fun j : Fin J => Lagrange.basis Finset.univ t j
    let Lambda := sSup ((fun s : ℝ => ∑ j : Fin J, |(ell j).eval s|) '' Set.Icc 0 h)
    let omega := fun i j : Fin J => ∫ s in 0..t i, (t i-s)*(ell j).eval s
    let positionWeight := omega ⟨J-1,by omega⟩
    let momentumWeight := fun j : Fin J => ∫ s in 0..h, (ell j).eval s
    let S := h^2/2*Lambda
    let a := Real.exp (-h/2)
    let sigma := Real.sqrt (1-Real.exp (-h))
    let gi := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin J => stdGaussian E)
    let γ := ((stdGaussian E).prod (stdGaussian E)).prod (gi.prod gi)
    let μ := ν.prod γ
    let MR := M + (1-Real.exp (-h)) * (Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let B := 6*MR + 3*eps^2 + 3*eta*(Module.finrank ℝ E : ℝ)
    let C := 2 + (1+Real.log ((1-c)⁻¹))/(-Real.log c)
    let L0 := C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (2*MR)/eps))
    let L1 := C*(1+Real.log (1+Real.sqrt (4*MR+2*S^2*B)/eps))
    h^2*Lambda ≤ 1 →
    ∃ p q : E → E, ∃ N : E → ℕ,
      Measurable p ∧ Measurable q ∧ Measurable N ∧
      (∀ y, p y + eta • gradient V (p y) = y ∧ ‖q y-p y‖ ≤ eps ∧
        ApproximateProximalExecution.proximalQuery (gradient V) eta eps y (N y+1) y =
          some (q y,N y+1)) ∧ LipschitzWith 1 p ∧
      let P0 := fun w : (E × E) × ((E × E) × ((Fin J → E) × (Fin J → E))) =>
        a • w.1.2 + sigma • w.2.1.1
      let Y0 := fun i w => w.1.1 + t i • P0 w
      let Z0 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y0 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
      let Y1 := fun i w => Y0 i w - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0 j w
      let Z1 := fun j w => gradient V (q (Y1 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
      let Φ := fun w => (w.1.1 + h • P0 w - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1 j w,
        a • (P0 w - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1 j w) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      let T := fun w => 2*J+∑ i, ((N (Y0 i w)+1)+(N (Y1 i w)+1))
      let Z0p := fun j w => gradient V (p (Y0 j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.1 j)
      let Y1p := fun i w => Y0 i w - ∑ j, omega i j • Z0p j w
      let Z1p := fun j w => gradient V (p (Y1p j w) + Real.sqrt eta • w.2.2.2 j)
      let Φp := fun w => (w.1.1 + h • P0 w - ∑ j, positionWeight j • Z1p j w,
        a • (P0 w - ∑ j, momentumWeight j • Z1p j w) + sigma • w.2.1.2)
      let W := fun (rho : ℝ) (μ ν : Measure (E × E)) =>
        (TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost
          (fun z : (E × E) × (E × E) =>
            (ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (‖z.1.1-z.2.1‖^2+‖z.1.2-z.2.2‖^2)))^rho)
          μ ν)^(rho⁻¹)
      Measurable Φ ∧ Measurable T ∧
      ∃ Kp Kq : Kernel (E × E) (E × E), IsMarkovKernel Kp ∧ IsMarkovKernel Kq ∧
      (∀ s, Kp s = γ.map (fun z => Φp (s,z))) ∧
      (∀ s, Kq s = γ.map (fun z => Φ (s,z))) ∧
      (∀ w, CountedPhaseProgram.phaseQuery (gradient V) eta eps h t omega positionWeight momentumWeight
        (fun y => N y+1) w = some (Φ w,T w)) ∧
      Integrable (fun w => (T w : ℝ)) μ ∧
      (∫ w, (T w : ℝ) ∂μ) ≤ (J : ℝ)*(2+L0+L1) ∧
      ∀ s rho, 1 ≤ rho → W rho (Kq s) (Kp s) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (3*h*Lambda*eps) := by
  classical
  dsimp only
  intro hstep
  obtain ⟨_,_,_,_,_,hLambda,_,_⟩ :=
    TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.ChebyshevLobattoQuadrature.chebyshev_lobatto_coefficients hJ hh
  have hh1 : h ≤ 1 := by
    have hsq : h^2 ≤ 1 := (le_mul_of_one_le_right (sq_nonneg h) hLambda).trans hstep
    nlinarith only [hsq,hh]
  have heta1 : eta < 1 := hec.trans_lt hc
  obtain ⟨p1,q1,N1,hp1,hq1,hN1,hall1,hPhi1,hT1,_,hrun1,hTI1,hcost1⟩ :=
    SourceQuadratureWork.source_quadrature_phase_work hJ hκ hV hH heta hec hc heps
      ν xstar hstar hh hh1 hM hstateI hstate
  obtain ⟨p2,q2,N2,hp2,hq2,hN2,hall2,hLip2,Kp,Kq,hKp,hKq,hKppush,hKqpush,hW,_⟩ :=
    ProximalPhaseStability.source_phase_proximal_stability hκ hV hH heta heta1 heps hJ hh hstep
  have hH' : ∀ x v : E, ((κ⁻¹ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ)*‖v‖^2 ≤
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ∧
      (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v) v ≤ (1 : ℝ≥0)*‖v‖^2 := by
    simpa only [NNReal.coe_inv,NNReal.coe_one,one_mul] using hH
  have hreg := TechnicalLemmas.Analysis.QuadraticRegularization.strongConvexOn_and_lipschitzWith_gradient_add_quadratic
    (r := 0) hV hH' (0 : E)
  have hg : LipschitzWith 1 (gradient V) := by simpa using hreg.2
  have hpEq : p1 = p2 := by
    funext y
    have hop1 := (hall1 y).1
    have hop2 := (hall2 y).1
    have hd : p1 y-p2 y = eta • (gradient V (p2 y)-gradient V (p1 y)) := by
      calc
        p1 y-p2 y = (p1 y+eta • gradient V (p1 y)) -
            (p2 y+eta • gradient V (p2 y)) +
            eta • (gradient V (p2 y)-gradient V (p1 y)) := by module
        _ = eta • (gradient V (p2 y)-gradient V (p1 y)) := by rw [hop1,hop2]; simp
    have hn : ‖p1 y-p2 y‖ ≤ eta*‖p1 y-p2 y‖ := by
      calc
        ‖p1 y-p2 y‖ = eta*‖gradient V (p2 y)-gradient V (p1 y)‖ := by
          rw [hd,norm_smul,Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_pos heta]
        _ ≤ eta*‖p1 y-p2 y‖ := by
          have hb := hg.norm_sub_le (p2 y) (p1 y)
          simpa only [NNReal.coe_one,one_mul,norm_sub_rev] using
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hb heta.le
    have hz : ‖p1 y-p2 y‖ = 0 := by
      nlinarith only [hn,norm_nonneg (p1 y-p2 y),heta1]
    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (norm_eq_zero.mp hz)
  have hpair (y : E) : (q1 y,N1 y+1) = (q2 y,N2 y+1) :=
    ProximalExecutionIdentity.successful_query_unique (gradient V) eta eps y
      (hall1 y).2.2 (hall2 y).2.2
  have hqEq : q1 = q2 := by funext y; exact congrArg Prod.fst (hpair y)
  have hNEq : N1 = N2 := by
    funext y
    exact Nat.add_right_cancel (congrArg Prod.snd (hpair y))
  subst p2
  subst q2
  subst N2
  exact ⟨p1,q1,N1,hp1,hq1,hN1,hall1,hLip2,hPhi1,hT1,Kp,Kq,hKp,hKq,
    hKppush,hKqpush,hrun1,hTI1,hcost1,hW⟩

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SmoothedPicardHMC.PhaseAccuracyWork

lesson.statement: There exist one measurable exact optimality map p, one measurable stopped output map q and one measurable N:E→Nat such that p(y)+eta*gradient V(p(y))=y, ||q(y)-p(y)||<=eps, p is nonexpansive and the actual residual-stopped interpreter from y returns some(q(y),N(y)+1) with sufficient fuel N(y)+1. The identical p,q,N define actual full-phase Markov Kp,Kq, the actual output Phi_q and the actual total returned gradient count T. For every state s and finite real rho>=1, true Euclidean W_rho(Kq(s),Kp(s))<=3hLambda eps. Under the same actual driving law mu=nu prod gamma, T is measurable, real-integrable and E_mu[T]<=J(2+L0+L1). For every driving input w the counted phase interpreter with fuel(y)=N(y)+1 returns exactly some(Phi_q(w),T(w)). All output/count/kernel/cost conjuncts share these witnesses.

steps.title: Discharge the genuine step adapter
steps.text: The compiled actual source coefficient certificate proves Lambda>=1. Combined with h>0 and h²Lambda<=1 it yields h²<=1 and h<=1. Thus the actual-work producer is callable with no new small-step premise.

steps.title: Obtain both genuine producers
steps.text: Use the actual source quadrature expected-work theorem for p_c,q_c,N_c and the precision theorem for p_a,q_a,N_a,Kp,Kq. Their gradient, eta, eps, starting state and all source arrays are identical; c may affect the certificate but never the interpreter. Both exact maps satisfy the genuine optimality equation.

steps.title: Identify the exact optimality map
steps.text: Derive 1-Lipschitz gradient from the actual C2 Hessian via the shared zero-quadratic specialization. Subtract the exact equations: the displacement equals eta times the reversed gradient displacement. Its norm is <=eta times itself; eta<1 forces zero. This proves p_c=p_a without assuming witness identity.

steps.title: Identify stopped points and returned counts
steps.text: Both successful calls use exactly the same residual branch norm(y-eta*g(x)-x)<=(1-eta)*eps, anchor y and starting x=y. Deterministic successful_query_unique identifies their returned point/count pairs independently of the supplied sufficient fuel. Take each projection and cancel +1 on natural counts; obtain q_c=q_a and N_c=N_a.
